title: Senior Backend Engineer
description:
About Us

Plentific is a property technology platform used by housing providers, local authorities, housing associations, asset managers, and contractors across the UK and Germany to coordinate repairs, maintenance, and contractor workflows at scale. The platform combines a marketplace, workflow automation, and operational analytics, and is built to handle the volume and compliance demands of social housing, local authority property portfolios, and large-scale residential operations.


We are headquartered in London and our team works across Europe.
We are growing the team to expand the platform's coverage across Europe and to integrate AI throughout the product and operating model. If you are interested in working on hard, real-world problems in a sector that has long been under-served by good software, we would like to hear from you.

The Role

This is a hands-on, fully remote role in one of Plentific's cross-functional product engineering teams. The Senior Backend Engineer works alongside product managers, frontend engineers, quality engineers, and other backend engineers to build and operate the services behind repairs, quoting and invoicing, payments, contractor search, messaging, notifications, and fraud prevention. The role is open across the European countries where we currently employ or engage remote engineers.


Our backend is built primarily in Python and Django, with Django REST Framework and FastAPI supporting APIs in a service-oriented architecture deployed on AWS and Kubernetes. PostgreSQL, Redis, and Celery underpin data-intensive and asynchronous workflows. title: Growth Lead
description:
About Nous

Nous is an AI agent that takes some of the load of life; making good decisions and acting for our users in areas where they’re not the experts or aren’t paying enough attention. We've started with optimising bills, where we're already saving households thousands, and are now expanding into new categories. Similar to how Amazon picked books as its first category and grew from there.

We’re growing fast, and it's working. 20x YoY growth makes us one of the fastest scaling startups in the UK. And NPS of +70 (higher than Apple) shows that our users love it.

We've just launched two more novel new products (on top of our existing bill optimisation). Insurance: we're the first to get the regulatory approval and build the tech to actually do the full insurance discovery and purchase journey as an agent for the user (not just give them a link to the best deal). Subscription management: lots of companies use Open Banking to draw pretty graphs – we're the first to use it to actively save people money starting by cancelling unwanted subscriptions for them.

It would be easy to look at this and think we've got it all figured out. But we've only scratched the surface; our ambitions are SO much higher.

We’re building a new category of product which is hard, so we’ve stacked the deck in our favour: an experienced founding team with multiple exits, and investors including the founders of Monzo, Wise, Booking.com, lastminute.com, Onfido, Funding Circle, Tide, Habito and more.

Still - the problems we’re solving are hard. ‘Talk is cheap’ applies to agents too. To have REAL impact, agents need to break out of the sandbox and take action in the real world where there are consequences. This means solving all the hard, thorny, interesting, frustrating problems the real world has to offer.

 

ABOUT THE ROLE

Nous is one of the UK’s fastest-growing, AI-native consumer start-ups. We’re looking for a commercially minded Growth Lead to help us continue to scale.

We're hiring now because a member of the team is going on maternity leave, but this isn't fixed-term cover. You'll start on influencer — our biggest acquisition channel — and we'll expect you to be leading a second growth area within your first year. When they return, the team will be bigger and so your remit will grow. Nous is scaling very fast, and what that second area is will depend on where the business needs you most by then.

We don’t expect you to have spent years in influencer marketing. You might come from B2B sales, partnerships, or another growth role where you’ve built a strong understanding of relationship management and what makes audiences take action. What matters is that you can apply that knowledge quickly.

Your goal will be performance, not brand or reach. You’ll be hands-on across the channel: finding creators, negotiating fees, writing briefs, reviewing content and managing campaigns. You’ll also help answer the bigger questions — who should we work with, what should we pay, what content converts, and how do we scale the channel profitably?

We’ve built internal tools to manage everything from creator outreach to performance and payments, and we’re constantly improving them. You don’t need to be an engineer, but you do need to be toolsy – using AI to automate repetitive work, improve processes and build better ways of working.

 

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Run influencer campaigns end-to-end — finding creators, outreach, negotiation, briefing, approvals and performance review.

  • Make commercial decisions — work out what creators are worth, negotiate fees and structure deals that make sense for us.

  • Create content that converts — write strong briefs and give clear feedback on creator content.

  • Own performance — understand how we’re tracking against volume and CAC targets and act when we’re falling behind.

  • Grow the channel — test new creators, propositions, platforms and approaches, then scale what works.

  • Make us more efficient — use AI, internal tools and better processes to reduce manual work as the channel grows.

ABOUT YOU

We’re open-minded about exactly where you’ve come from. You might come from B2B sales, affiliates, partnerships or another performance-focused growth role.

You’ll likely thrive here if:

  • You have relevant hands-on experience. You’ve been part of a successful partnerships-led growth team. If you have not worked with creators before you can pick up the specifics of influencer marketing quickly.

  • You’re commercially minded and numerate. You’re comfortable negotiating and working with CAC, conversion rates, budgets and targets.

  • You care about performance. You’re more interested in whether content drove customers than whether it got lots of views.

  • You have good creative judgement. You know what makes social content engaging, credible and persuasive.

  • You understand social media. You have a strong feel for creators, audiences and what makes content work on platforms like Instagram, TikTok and YouTube.

  • You can move quickly without sacrificing quality. You’re comfortable juggling priorities and making decisions in a fast-moving environment.

  • You’re resourceful and toolsy. You naturally look for better ways of doing things and use AI to automate work, analyse data and improve processes.

  • You’re happy in a start-up. You’re comfortable taking ownership, figuring things out and adapting as the company grows.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Across energy, mobile, broadband, insurance and subscriptions, Nous has grown 20x in the last 12 months. Our reporting hasn't always kept pace. We're hiring a Head of Business Intelligence to own this and fix it.

That means you'll set the standards rather than inherit them. No legacy team, no committee, no five-year-old semantic layer you're not allowed to touch. Which cuts both ways.

Take our unit economics. Revenue per household is a commercial assumption rather than a column in a table, and it varies as a function of behaviour, service lines managed, engagement. Some users are Premium, some not; some suppliers pay a bounty per switch, some pay nothing. Households change providers, cancel services, then switch again, and their value compounds over time in a complex way. Getting from a decent estimate to a genuinely defensible view of LTV, payback and cohort behaviour is one of the highest-leverage things anyone could do here, and it's the kind of problem that has no textbook answer.

To get there you'll own the data foundations too: canonical definitions of our fundamental metrics, the dbt models underneath them, and the reporting that Growth, Commercial, Operations and Finance depend on. We've built quickly and there's real judgment and craft required to make that as solid as the business now requires but doing so in a scrappy and pragmatic way.

You'd work directly with the senior team: CEO, Head of Finance, and the Growth, Commercial, Operations and Product leads. Your work is what the board sees. Our current stack is Postgres replicated into Snowflake via Fivetran, dbt for transformation, Omni for modelling and dashboards, Amplitude for product analytics, and Statsig for experimentation, plus a growing set of bespoke dashboarding and reporting instrumentation.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Own the canonical definitions. Sponsor an agreed definition for each fundamental metric. Then hold the line intelligently when someone wants a subtly different version for their deck.

  • Own the models underneath. Our dbt and Omni models have grown alongside the business, and there's a satisfying piece of work in consolidating them, moving everything onto our current event standard, and retiring what's no longer earning its place.

  • Make the numbers provable. Events, database tables and the finance ledger should agree, and you'd build the reconciliation and automated checks that keep them agreeing as we scale.

  • Make self-serve work properly. A clean semantic layer, sensible naming, documentation people actually read, and a small set of dashboards trusted enough that nobody builds their own version on the side.

  • Own commercial reporting and unit economics: revenue per switch by product and supplier, contribution margin, CAC and payback by channel, cohort retention, repeat switching, LTV. Partner with Finance on management reporting, the board pack, and the reporting infrastructure behind investor updates.

  • Be the analytical partner to the commercial teams. Growth needs to know which channels work. Commercial needs to know which supplier deals are worth doing. Operations needs to know where the process leaks. Answer those questions, then build the reporting that stops them being asked again.

  • Set the governance: access, PII handling, how deleted users are treated in analytics, what can and can't leave an aggregate. Plus the commercial side of the data stack itself, since pipeline spend at our scale is worth someone owning properly.

  • Continue to drive the use of AI. Most of our analytical work now happens in Claude Code alongside SQL. We'd expect you to continue to push this hard..

ABOUT YOU

You're the person who noticed the number was wrong. Somewhere you've worked, there was a metric everybody quoted that didn't survive contact with the underlying data, and you were the one who found it, worked out why, and fixed it properly instead of adding a footnote.

You'll likely thrive in this role if:

  • You're commercially minded as well as technically strong. You can build the model, and you have a view on what it says. When you present a cohort curve you have an opinion about what we should do about it.

  • You're fussy about correctness in a way other people find slightly excessive. You triangulate. You reconcile. You won't ship a chart you can't defend, and you're comfortable pushing back on a number senior people have grown attached to, because you've already checked it three ways.

  • You've done this from scratch. You've walked into a fast-growing company where the reporting was held together with string and made it solid. You know what order to do it in, and which bits can wait.

  • You're hands-on and expect to stay that way. You'll be writing the SQL and building the models yourself for a good while. We keep the middle thin on purpose.

  • You simplify. Faced with forty dashboards, your instinct is to work out which six matter and kill the rest. You'd rather have a few things everyone trusts than a complete set nobody opens.

  • You build with AI tools daily. Not "I've tried ChatGPT". You use Claude Code or similar as part of how you actually work: writing and debugging SQL, navigating an unfamiliar schema, automating your own checks.

ESSENTIAL EXPERIENCE

  • Substantial experience in analytics, BI or data leadership, including a spell owning the numbers for a fast-growing consumer or transactional business. We care more about what you've built than the years attached to it.

  • Confident SQL. Handed an unfamiliar schema, you can get to a defensible answer without help.

  • Hands-on with a modern warehouse (Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift or similar) and a transformation layer (dbt or equivalent). You've written and maintained the models, not just commissioned them.

  • Hands-on with a BI and semantic modelling tool (Omni, Looker, Lightdash, Metabase, Power BI, Tableau), including designing the semantic layer rather than only building charts on top of someone else's.

  • Event analytics (Amplitude, Mixpanel, GA4 or similar), and a working understanding of where event data and database data disagree and why.

  • A track record of establishing metric definitions and getting an organisation to actually adopt them. That's as much a persuasion problem as a technical one.

  • Comfort working directly with finance on management reporting and reconciliation.

  • Active use of AI tooling in your day-to-day work.

DESIRABLE EXPERIENCE

  • Consumer subscription, marketplace, fintech, energy or utilities. Anywhere with messy third-party data and revenue that isn't a clean row in a table.

  • Modelling LTV, payback and cohort behaviour where the inputs are commercial assumptions rather than observed values, and being clear-eyed about the uncertainty that creates.

  • Experimentation platforms (Statsig, Optimizely, GrowthBook) and reading experiment results honestly.

  • Board and investor reporting.

  • Instrumentation and tracking plan design, including working with engineers to get events fired in the right places and keep them there.

  • Some Python for the analysis that doesn't fit in SQL.

  • You've built your own tools when the ones available weren't good enough.

REMUNERATION AND BENEFITS

  • Compelling packages, including share options with life-changing upside. We've raised enough money to pay real salaries. We're building something great together and we all share in the upside. If we win, we win together.

  • An environment where you can do your best work:

How we build (worth reading before the role)

Most companies split the thinkers, the doers and the builders. We don't. Something special happens when they're the same people: a small team that builds and owns the tools for its own problems understands those problems from the inside. So the rule at Nous is simple. The person who feels the problem should be the one who builds the fix.

This isn't brand new. A sharp generalist could always wire something together with no-code and low-code tools to solve a problem. The catch was the ceiling: those tools were far more limited than real code, so you hit a wall the moment the problem got interesting. Unless you had superhuman levels of stubbornness and a high tolerance for using tools for things they really weren't designed for. What's changed is that ceiling. With AI tooling and a lot of context, you're now building much closer to real code, and shipping it on the live product. You can change how our WhatsApp agent handles a tricky conversation, dig through Open Banking data to find money we should be saving people, prototype a feature, or automate a process that used to eat someone's week.

And you're not doing this around engineering, you're doing it alongside engineers. Engineers build the safe surfaces you ship on (the tools, the infrastructure, the context APIs, the guardrails), and they're who you pull in when you reach the edge of what's safe to touch alone.

None of that works without a particular kind of person: not a software engineer, but someone who builds like one.

The role

You'll own a product surface and make it better, end to end, without waiting for an engineer to do it for you.

The clearest version of this already exists on the team. Ben joined as a PM, not an engineer. Engineering set him up with the right infrastructure and a context API, and now he ships changes to Nora (our customer-facing WhatsApp agent) himself, pulling people in only when he's blocked.

Worth being upfront: we've never hired for this profile directly before. The people doing it today grew into it here (Ben from product, Gen from ops) once we set them up with the tooling and context to build. You'd be the first we bring in, so expect the role to shift a bit as we figure out what works.

Depending on where you're strongest and where we need you most, the first surface might be:

  • Nora and our AI agents. Find where she struggles in real conversations, improve how she handles them, build and run the evals that tell us whether she's getting better, and tighten the recovery flows for when things go wrong.

  • Open Banking and subscriptions. Dig into the data behind our subscription product, spot the patterns, and build the logic that decides what's worth cancelling or flagging. Then work out how we cancel them automatically. Real money back in people's pockets.

  • Whatever's most broken. New products and surfaces appear constantly. You'll take a rough, messy problem and turn it into something shipped and improving.

What you'll actually do

  • Take a product problem from rough to shipped, with AI tooling (Claude Code, Cursor, whatever gets it done) as your main working environment.

  • Answer your own questions. When you need to know how many members hit a broken flow last week, write the query and find out. Don't file a ticket and wait.

  • Ship on the safe surfaces: prompts, agent behaviour, configuration, workflows, data pipelines, internal tools. Know where the edge is, and pull in an engineer before you cross it.

  • Live close to the user. Read the conversations, watch where the product delights people or falls over, and let that drive what you build next.

  • Own the outcome. A feature isn't done when you've shipped it, it's done when it's working for members.

About you

You build without precise instructions. You've been a founder, an early PM, or the generalist who ends up owning the thing nobody else will. Give you a problem and some context and you start building. You don't wait for a spec or a map.

AI tooling is already how you work. Not "ChatGPT wrote my cover letter". You use Claude Code, Cursor or similar as your working environment: prototyping, querying data, navigating systems, automating your own work. title: Product Engineer (all levels)
description:
👋 Hi, I’m Sina, CTO at Nous. 

I’ve spent my entire career in startups, starting my first company when I was a teenager, and navigated many 0→1 journeys (including starting the largest social network of its time in my home country).

The common thread that led me here is finding complexity that wastes people’s time or money, then solving for making them disappear. And that’s exactly what Nous aims to do.

If this problem space resonates, please read on. 

PS: I’ve actually written this page with my hands; this is not AI-written content!

About Nous

Roughly 90% of UK households are overpaying on their bills. Nous is an agent to absorb complexity out of households, saving them money and time. Our mission is to make people’s lives simpler and fairer, starting with the 30 million households here in the UK, and soon far beyond.

Nous is growing fast, and it’s working. 20x YoY growth makes us one of the fastest scaling startups in the UK. And NPS of +70 (higher than Apple) shows that our users love it.

We’ve just launched two novel new products (on top of our current service lines). Insurance: we’re the first to get the regulatory approval and build the tech to actually do the full insurance discovery and purchase journey as an agent for the user (not just give them a link to the best deal). Subscription management: lots of companies use open banking to draw pretty graphs - we’re the first to use it to actively save people money starting by cancelling unwanted subscriptions for them.

It would be easy to look at this and think we’ve got it all figured out.

But we’ve only scratched the surface; our ambitions are SO much higher. We started with bills because ‘change begins at home’ - it’s a naturally low-interest, messy area of our lives which most of us don’t want to think about. Similar to how Amazon started with books as their first category to go after.

‘Talk is cheap. Action is what really matters’. What we’re building is an agent to take some of the load of life, make good decisions and act for us in areas we can’t or don’t want to act on our own. For an agent, advice is cheap. Action is the product. And action means solving problems in the messy real world.

A note on product

There’s ‘product’ as in the web application that guides our users through the complex world of bills and household admin. It acts as their interface to our management service, as well as all the behind the scenes capabilities needed to orchestrate and deliver that service - actually saving our users money and time. Try it here: app.nous.co/signup (it’s free!)

Then there’s ‘product’ as experienced by our users - which is a service which makes life simple and fair. To deliver this we’ve built a set of powerful capabilities that let us run and improve the service efficiently at scale: agentic communication, multimodal data extraction, orchestration for long-running operational processes, recommendations, our own agentic harness, and more. We compose these into executable workflows that deliver real outcomes for members, like switching someone to a better energy deal without the hassle.

Today, we help manage six areas of household spending: Energy, Mobile, Broadband, Mortgage, Personal finances (e.g., managing subscriptions), and Insurance. But we’re just getting started. Behind the scenes, we’ve built the technology (we call it Blueprints) that acts as rails for us to quickly expand on the breadth and depth of our service lines.

The role

We need your help building a world-class product that will be used regularly by millions of people; which means figuring out, together, what it really takes to absorb household complexity.

As a product engineer, we'll empower you with context to enable fast iterations, end-to-end ownership and lots of agency. You’ll be a hands-on technical leader on some of the highest-leverage areas of our codebase, from building out agentic capabilities to scaling our service logic.

Some examples of the types of problems you'll solve:

  • Anton led and shipped an entire product line around open banking and subscription management three months after joining. Yes, he had support from legal, design, commercial and his team (we even became FCA registered). But one product engineer still took it from idea to a best-in-class product in the category.

  • Ed led the our latest Blueprint architecture, which now powers every service line. Changes to complex, long-running workflows that once took weeks can now sometimes take minutes. All safely, reliably and with full type safety.

  • Tim led and shipped our car insurance product line, in less than 3 months. We built a journey where an agent performs the discovery and purchase journeys - something that's not been done before and needed problem solving at the intersection of engineering, product and regulatory.

  • As a team, we built our own agentic harness (we call it super-engineer); it’s enabled us to build faster, investigate complex cross-system issues effectively; and it self-improves.

There are also so many interesting problems we are in the infancy of solving. Just as an example - user’s trust us with their Open Banking data - but it’s just lists of transactions. How can we use that stream of information and combine it with all the other data we have, to reduce friction from their lives?

Every week, we’re building tools for ourselves and evolving how we work, to make ourselves more effective. I strongly believe in the value of compounding gains, and much of our focus goes into investing in what results in exponential growth.


Although our stack is constantly evolving (and you can help shape that), here’s a current snapshot:

  • Full-stack TypeScript, React, Postgres, and Temporal for long-running orchestration.

  • Infra: AWS, Terraform, strong observability via Sentry and Datadog (full-stack, not just logs).

  • Data: we lean heavily on Snowflake, Omni, dbt, Fivetran, Amplitude and Segment — and we’ve even built some of our own tooling to understand how well we’re helping our members.

  • And we use Github, Linear, Graphite, and Blacksmith every day. We choose the best tool for the job, and don’t obsess around specific technologies.

  • We also heavily rely on our wide range of agentic and tooling harness that we build and iterate on across the team. They’re part of the “secret” behind how we move fast, reliably.

You’ll report directly to the CTO (and we’ll work closely), so will be in the room for key architectural and product decisions. We’re deliberately light on layers of management: exceptional individual contributors shape direction by solving hard problems.


We organise around small product squads (around 5–7 people) with a single shared objective; and ship and learn fast.

You'll build in two modes

This is the bit that makes the role different, so it's worth being clear about.

Sometimes you build the product directly. That might mean a new product line, a core product improvement; or an exciting new idea to experiment on the product. You're usually working with one or two others, moving fast from a rough plan and jumping on problems as they surface.

Sometimes you build the multiplier. The safe surfaces and shared tooling that let a non-engineer ship without breaking things. Think the internal equivalent of what Lovable did for "anyone can put a website live", but for our problems: bills, switching, household admin at scale.

Both are hard engineering work. And the two feed each other: the better the multiplier you build, the more the genuinely deep problems are the ones left for you. Leverage for the ops team is leverage for you.

What we look for

You don't need to tick every box. If you read these and feel a mix of "this is me" and "this would stretch me", you're probably right for it.

  • You own problems end to end. You're happiest going from fuzzy pain to shipped fix to the numbers that show it worked. You instinctively ask "what's the smallest thing we can ship to learn?" instead of waiting for a perfect spec.

  • You think like a PM as much as an engineer. You care about the problem, the user, flow, UX, and even copy as much as correctness, because you've seen a small wording change flip confusion into action.

  • You're a pragmatic builder. Clean, practical code others can extend. You know when to abstract and when to keep it brutally simple to go fast. You'll happily delete your own code when reality disagrees with it.

  • You build leverage for other people. You explain complex things simply, you pair on gnarly problems, and you leave things clearer than you found them. You see a good tool that unblocks a teammate as real work, not a distraction from it.

  • You're here for the problem. Fairness, money and complexity, made manageable for people who don't have time to fight the system themselves. You'd rather work hard on something that genuinely helps.

We hire across all levels (mid-senior, to staff+), with a minimum 2 years of professional experience. The size and independence of your initial scope will reflect your experience, but the shape of the role is the same: you own outcomes. For earlier-career candidates, our assessment is primarily on your growth trajectory.

This probably isn't for you if…

  • You want a clear remit handed down before you can move. Here you get lots of context and invested colleagues, not a manager translating the work into tickets for you.

  • You believe nothing should ship unless it routes through a gate you personally control. The control we care about is structural: guardrails in the tools, not who's allowed to type. If that sounds too loose, we'll probably frustrate each other.

  • You want to specialise narrowly and stay in one layer. The role is broad by design.

What to expect

As CTO, and the person hiring for this role, you can hold me to these promises:

  • You’ll never be bored. You’ll continuously have difficult and interesting challenges to solve

  • The rest of the team and I will empower you with context, and will involve you as a co-founder

  • You’ll be learning every day, solve new challenges, and sometimes find yourself running while simultaneously learning how to run

  • You’ll have the space and support to grow your AI engineering skills, whether through harness engineering, trying new approaches, or even going as far as inventing new ways of solving problems. We’re building at the edge of what is possible, and we are conscious that there’s trial and error and first principles thinking involved in figuring it out

  • You’ll work closely with a caring and highly intelligent team. It’s ok, stalk us on Linkedin and check for yourself

Remuneration and benefits

Compelling packages, including meaningful share options with life-changing upside. We’ve raised enough money to pay real salaries. We're building something great together and we all share in the upside. If we win, we win together.

  • ☕ Very good coffee

  • 🍽️ A well-stocked kitchen (featuring a wildly popular toastie maker) so you can always make yourself a breakfast or light lunch on the house

  • 🎉 Informal social every week, something bigger every month, plus a set-piece event in the summer and again at Christmas - we're not robots!

UFORCE exists to make aggression unaffordable.

Founded in Ukraine and headquartered in London, UFORCE is a defence-technology company with operations across Europe, the United States and Asia.

UFORCE builds uncrewed vessels, ground robotics and aircraft, autonomy software, and the command-and-control layer that operates them together. Each platform is deployable on its own, and stronger as part of the system. Its product lines include the MAGURA family of uncrewed surface vessels, the NEMESIS family of strike platforms, the LIUT family of ground robotic platforms, and counter-UAS systems.

About the role

The Project Manager, Business Operations owns cross-functional work that does not yet have a natural owner. You will take problems that are undefined, unscoped, and unassigned and turn them into well-managed projects with a clear sponsor, an agreed outcome, and a documented close.

This is not a traditional project management role with a fixed portfolio. Your work will be allocated on a rolling basis by the VP of Business Operations based on the company’s most important emerging needs. You may document and implement an M&A process, build leadership reporting dashboards, introduce new business systems and processes, or coordinate a training program across multiple regions.

The common thread is ambiguity: you will bring structure, ownership, and momentum to important work that might otherwise stall between functions.

What you’ll do

  • Take ambiguous business problems and translate them into clearly scoped projects with defined outcomes, owners, milestones, and completion criteria.

  • Lead multiple concurrent cross-functional projects from initial definition through execution, handover, and documented close.

  • Establish alignment among stakeholders who may have different priorities and do not report to you.

  • Identify the right sponsor and contributors for each project and establish clear responsibilities before execution begins.

  • Build and document operational processes where no established approach currently exists.

  • Influence teams to adopt new processes, systems, or ways of working.

  • Own an agreed share of leadership and business reporting, producing concise, decision-ready updates without requiring follow-up.

  • Prioritize competing requests from senior stakeholders and communicate trade-offs clearly.

  • Surface risks, resolve blockers, and exercise sound judgment about what to handle independently and when to escalate.

  • Ensure completed projects transition to a named long-term owner with the documentation and processes required to sustain them.

  • Use AI tools thoughtfully to accelerate research, analysis, documentation, and day-to-day project delivery.

What we’re looking for

  • Demonstrated ability to take an undefined problem and create a practical, executable plan without waiting for a detailed brief.

  • Experience delivering cross-functional projects through stakeholders over whom you have no direct authority.

  • Strong judgment and the ability to operate independently in a fast-moving environment where processes and governance are still being built.

  • Evidence of creating systems, processes, or operating practices that continued after your direct involvement ended.

  • Ability to manage multiple competing priorities and make clear trade-offs when demand exceeds capacity.

  • Confidence working with senior stakeholders, including navigating disagreement and resistance constructively.

  • Excellent written communication, with the ability to produce concise, leadership-ready materials that require minimal revision.

  • Strong attention to accountability, including clear ownership, deadlines, success measures, and documented project closure.

  • Practical fluency with AI tools, including sound judgment about where their outputs can and cannot be trusted.

Nice to have

  • Previous experience in a PMO, business operations, program management, or management consulting environment.

  • Experience working directly with executives or senior external clients.

  • Experience using Notion or comparable project and knowledge-management platforms.

  • Experience documenting processes and authoring standard operating procedures.

  • Exposure to Ukraine or experience in defense, dual-use technology, regulated industries, or government-adjacent environments.

title: Staff AI Engineer
description:
UFORCE exists to make aggression unaffordable.

Founded in Ukraine and headquartered in London, UFORCE is a defence-technology company with operations across Europe, the United States and Asia.

UFORCE builds uncrewed vessels, ground robotics and aircraft, autonomy software, and the command-and-control layer that operates them together. Each platform is deployable on its own, and stronger as part of the system. Its product lines include the MAGURA family of uncrewed surface vessels, the NEMESIS family of strike platforms, the LIUT family of ground robotic platforms, and counter-UAS systems.

About the role

The Staff Engineer, AI / ML — Self-Serve Toolchain will build the end-to-end system that lets customers adapt UFORCE models on their own private data without exposing that data to us.

This role spans data processing, foundation-model-assisted labeling, human-in-the-loop QA, active learning, training, evaluation, and model promotion. You will turn an in-flight principal-led capability into a repeatable toolchain that non-expert customers can run safely on-site.

What you’ll do

 

  • Own the ML adaptation pipeline from raw customer data to trained, evaluated, deployable models.

  • Build foundation-model-assisted labeling workflows using tools such as SAM-2, Grounding DINO, open-vocabulary models, LLM steering, and human review.

  • Design self-serve operator workflows using yes/no/maybe feedback and natural-language corrections.

  • Create versioned datasets with lineage, data cards, label provenance, class distributions, and known gaps.

  • Build QA methods that catch systematic pseudo-label errors, missing annotations, and long-tail data gaps.

  • Develop active-learning loops that prioritize the highest-value frames for limited operator review.

  • Build reproducible train/eval pipelines with experiment tracking, model packaging, and promotion gates.

  • Design evaluation around held-out anchor sets, leakage prevention, baselines, slice metrics, and automated approve/reject decisions.

  • Package the toolchain for on-prem, air-gapped, regulated, or customer-held environments.

  • Close the field-failure loop by feeding live failures back into the next tune cycle.

  • Lead and grow a small specialist team around curation, auto-labeling, deployment, and onboarding.

What success looks like

 

  • Customers can run a full adaptation cycle without engineer intervention.

  • Customer data stays inside the customer boundary.

  • The system produces trusted datasets with clear provenance and quality signals.

  • Pseudo-label quality is measured and systematic errors are caught early.

  • The promotion gate can approve or reject models based on evidence, not intuition.

  • Evaluation is protected by anchor sets, leakage controls, slice metrics, and baseline comparisons.

  • Field failures become reproducible inputs to the next training cycle.

  • Synthetic data is used only when it proves value against real held-out data.

  • The toolchain becomes a repeatable capability supported by a small, ramped team.

Required Qualifications

 

  • 5+ years building production ML, AI, or computer-vision systems.

  • Strong Python and PyTorch.

  • Experience owning ML data pipelines, training pipelines, or evaluation infrastructure.

  • Deep CV data experience: detection, segmentation, annotation taxonomies, dataset curation, and data quality.

  • Hands-on experience with model-in-the-loop or foundation-model-assisted labeling.

  • Familiarity with tools such as SAM-2, Grounding DINO, FiftyOne, and annotation platforms.

  • Strong understanding of evaluation: held-out sets, leakage prevention, baselines, slice metrics, and promotion gates.

  • Experience with QA sampling, label-noise analysis, missing annotations, IAA, or alternatives when only one operator is available.

  • Experience with active learning or other methods for prioritizing labeling effort.

  • Ability to reason about dataset economics: quality vs. quantity, long-tail coverage, and cost-per-useful-example.

  • Experience with dataset versioning, lineage, experiment tracking, model registries, or data cards.

  • Strong ownership, communication, and systems thinking.

  • Experience leading engineers as a tech lead, staff engineer, or small-team manager.

Nice to have

 

  • Synthetic data, sim2real, or domain randomization experience.

  • EO / IR / LWIR, remote sensing, maritime imagery, or small-object detection experience.

  • Privacy-preserving ML, federated learning, on-prem, or air-gapped deployment experience.

  • Experience building self-serve ML platforms or tools for non-expert users.

  • Experience with lakeFS, DVC, MLflow, Weights & Biases, Kubernetes, Kubeflow, Flyte, Dagster, Airflow, or Argo.

  • LLM application, context engineering, structured output, or LLM evaluation experience.

  • Exposure to radar, AIS, EO/IR fusion, tracking, sensor fusion, robotics, autonomy, UxV, defence tech, C2/C4ISR, or tactical systems.

  • You’ll learn to quickly capture attention on the fly, both by mastering cold calling or through hyper-personalized email and LinkedIn messages.

How we work at Numeric

  •  We are an in-person company. We believe that when things are moving quickly, working in-person is key to providing everyone with context, adapting, and, well, it’s more fun this way

—

title: Agentic Compiler Engineer
description:
ABOUT KOG

Kog builds a co-designed inference stack for real-time AI agents on standard datacenter GPUs, spanning model architecture, inference engine, compilers, and low-level GPU kernels.

On the model side, we developed Laneformer 2B and Delayed Tensor Parallelism (DTP), a Transformer architecture that overlaps communication with useful computation and weight streaming.

On the systems side, the Kog Inference Engine runs this stack on standard AMD and NVIDIA datacenter GPUs.

Kog generates 3,500 tokens/s per request on 8 AMD MI300X GPUs and 2,100 tokens/s per request on 8 NVIDIA H200 GPUs, in FP16 at batch size 1, with quantization and speculative decoding disabled.

Our next major project is AGCO, our agentic compiler. AGCO is designed to optimize LLMs across different GPUs and optimization targets, including very fast inference.

The team has 10 people, including 9 engineers and researchers and 4 PhDs.

Test it at playground.kog.ai. Read the technical details on the Kog Labs blog.

 

WHAT YOU WILL WORK ON

You will work directly on AGCO.

The goal is to build a system that can explore ways to optimize LLM execution, generate changes, compile them, check correctness, run them on real hardware, measure the results, and use this feedback to guide the next optimization.

You will contribute to areas such as:

  • Compiler and IR design for representing and transforming LLM computations.

  • Optimization passes, lowering, and code generation.

  • Search methods for exploring different implementations and execution strategies.

  • Verification and correctness checks for generated changes.

  • GPU execution, profiling, and performance optimization.

  • LLM inference across operators, memory, parallelism, and communication.

  • Optimization loops that connect generated changes to measurements on real GPUs.

One direction we are exploring combines an IR, a verifier, a compiler, and a search optimizer. We plan to start with focused problems, build working prototypes, and extend the system from what we learn.

Your main area will depend on your experience, skills, and interests. You may focus more on compilers, GPU systems, or LLM inference while working closely with people across the full stack.

 

WHAT WE LOOK FOR

We look for engineers with deep technical expertise and original work in at least one area relevant to AGCO.

Relevant experience includes:

  • Compiler engineering, including optimization passes, IRs, lowering, code generation, LLVM, or MLIR.

  • GPU programming with CUDA, HIP, Metal, Vulkan, or similar technologies.

  • GPU performance work involving kernels, memory, synchronization, profiling, or hardware behavior.

  • LLM inference engines and performance optimization.

  • Attention, MoE, parallelism, communication, or other systems-level parts of LLM execution.

  • Formal verification, equivalence checking, SAT/SMT, or related methods.

  • Systems that generate, search, test, benchmark, or optimize code automatically.

We care about what you personally built and the technical decisions behind it. Strong candidates can explain the problem, their approach, the alternatives they explored, and how they measured the result.

We review technical work during the process. This can be public code, an upstream contribution, a paper, a thesis, a technical project, or a detailed write-up based on work you can share.

 

WHAT WE OFFER

You will join a small team building AGCO as a core part of Kog's technology.

  • Work at the intersection of compilers, GPU systems, and LLM inference.

  • Direct access to engineers working across the full inference stack.

  • A fast loop from an optimization idea to compilation, execution, verification, and measurement on real GPUs.

  • The opportunity to go deep in your strongest technical area while expanding into the other parts of the stack.

  • High ownership over technical decisions and systems that will shape how Kog optimizes LLM inference.

This role is based in Paris, and we are looking for candidates who can relocate to Paris and work closely with the team.

title: Responsable bourses et mobilité internationale F/H
description:
Vos missions

Vous assurez la gestion des dispositifs de financement de la mobilité internationale des étudiants et des personnels et contribuez au pilotage de celui-ci.

Vous garantissez la qualité, la conformité et le suivi administratif et financier des dispositifs de bourses, notamment dans le cadre du programme Erasmus+.

En complément de cette mission principale, vous contribuez à la mise en œuvre des engagements de l’UTC dans le cadre de la Charte Erasmus+ et de ses grandes priorités, inclusion et diversité, transition écologique, transformation numérique, participation à la vie démocratique et aux valeurs européennes.

Dans ce cadre, vous participez au développement d’actions à destination des étudiants et des personnels : événements, actions de sensibilisation, formations courtes, ressources et formations en ligne.

En tant que référent-e « Transition numérique » Erasmus+ de la DRI, vous accompagnez également la transformation numérique des processus de mobilité et participez activement au déploiement, au paramétrage fonctionnel et à l’appropriation du logiciel de gestion de la mobilité internationale et des partenariats universitaires au sein de la DRI.

Dans le cadre du déploiement de cet outil à l’UTC, vous participez à la transformation et à la dématérialisation des processus de gestion de la mobilité internationale.

À ce titre, vous contribuez notamment au/à l’:

  • Déploiement de la solution numérique : analyse des processus existants, workflows, tests, paramétrage…

  • Amélioration régulière : cohérence, fiabilité des données, évolution

  • Accompagnement des membres du service : prise en main, tutoriels

  • Développement d’une utilisation experte progressive : indicateurs et suivi… 

Vous participez ainsi à faire de la solution numérique un outil d’amélioration et de transformation des processus. 

3. Contribuer à la mise en œuvre des priorités de la Charte Erasmus+

Contribuer à la déclinaison opérationnelle des engagements de l’UTC dans le cadre de la Charte Erasmus+ et de ses quatre grandes priorités :

  • Inclusion et diversité : favoriser l’accès à la mobilité des publics ayant moins d’opportunités et améliorer leur accompagnement.

  • Transition écologique : promouvoir une mobilité internationale plus responsable et sensibiliser aux enjeux environnementaux.

  • Transformation numérique : développer les usages et ressources numériques liés à la mobilité et accompagner la dématérialisation des dispositifs Erasmus+.

  • Participation et citoyenneté européenne : développer des actions favorisant la connaissance de l’Europe, de ses valeurs et des opportunités offertes par Erasmus+. 

4. Contribuer à la promotion des actions et événements à destination des étudiants

Contribuer à la promotion de la mobilité internationale et des priorités Erasmus+ :

5. Contribuer au développement des formations courtes et des ressources pédagogiques

Contribuer à la conception et à l’animation de formations courtes, ateliers et ressources pédagogiques, en présentiel, en ligne ou en format hybride, dans le contexte de la mission (tutoriels et ressources numériques destinés aux étudiants et personnels).

Participer, selon les besoins, aux projets transversaux de la Direction aux Relations Internationales : projets Erasmus+, alliance européenne SUNRISE, événements internationaux, actions de promotion de la mobilité, internationalisation des formations et démarches d’amélioration continue

title: FPGA Engineer - Electronic Warfare
description:
About Alta Ares


Alta Ares is an air defense Neoprime. We build AI-guided interceptors to counter drones and cruise missiles, along with the software platform that powers them.

Our customers are NATO-aligned militaries and defense institutions, and our systems are regularly deployed during live exercises and operational demonstrations across Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.

Founded in 2024, we have grown to 90 people, raised over $60M, and increased revenue 40× this year. We are now entering a new phase of international expansion, industrial scaling, fundraising, and product development.

Role & Mission

  • Own the development of FPGA functions for our electronic warfare and signals intelligence capabilities, from initial architecture to validation on operational hardware.

  • Work with systems and algorithm engineers to define processing requirements and assess implementation feasibility.

  • Build RTL modules in VHDL or SystemVerilog to process digitized RF signals, extract relevant information, and generate waveforms.

  • Adapt and validate DSP algorithms for FPGA implementation, balancing numerical accuracy, processing speed, and hardware resources.

  • Integrate acquisition and processing chains, including digital down-conversion, filtering, channelization, FFT, detection, direction-finding, and classification.

  • Establish verification methods and testbenches to check functional behavior and performance throughout development.

  • Connect programmable logic to RF converters and embedded processors, defining data transfers, control interfaces, clocking, and synchronization.

  • Resolve implementation constraints, achieve timing closure, and optimize resource utilization and power consumption.

  • Bring up FPGA designs on target boards, investigate integration issues, and correlate measured behavior with simulation results.

  • Contribute to laboratory and field testing alongside RF, software, and systems engineers.

  • Maintain clear design records, interface specifications, and validation evidence.

  • Improve reusable FPGA components and development practices as the product portfolio grows.

Candidate Profile

  • MSc in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Signal Processing, or a related field.

  • Strong experience developing and verifying RTL in VHDL or SystemVerilog, with a focus on digital signal processing.

  • Practical experience implementing designs on SoC FPGAs, including synthesis, implementation, timing analysis, and hardware debugging.

  • Strong understanding of sampled signals, frequency conversion, digital filtering, spectral analysis, and fixed-point numerical behavior.

  • Ability to reason across FPGA, processor, and RF hardware boundaries when making design decisions.

  • Experience modelling algorithms and comparing reference models with hardware results; familiarity with MATLAB, Simulink, Python, or HLS is a plus.

  • Familiarity with RF measurements and laboratory equipment, including spectrum analyzers, signal generators, and oscilloscopes, is a plus.

  • Prior experience in electronic warfare is welcome but not required.


Skills & Qualities

  • Hands-on engineer who enjoys taking designs from simulation to working hardware.

  • Methodical approach to debugging, with the ability to isolate problems across complex signal chains.

  • Able to own a technical scope independently and communicate progress, risks, and trade-offs clearly.

  • Rigorous approach to verification, documentation, and design traceability.

  • Comfortable collaborating across disciplines and adapting to evolving product requirements.

  • Entrepreneurial mindset with the ability to operate autonomously in a fast-growing company.

  • High integrity and professionalism in handling sensitive defense technologies.

title: Photonic Packaging Engineer
description:
About Quandela

Quandela is a global leader in photonic quantum computing, developing hardware and software technologies to build scalable and energy-efficient quantum systems.

With more than 140 people, we develop our own stack, from semiconductor quantum emitters and photonic integrated circuits to quantum control systems, software and algorithms.

Our ambition is to build large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computers. Reaching this scale requires increasingly reliable, manufacturable and integrated photonic hardware, making our Integrated Photonics team a key part of this journey.

About this position:

You will join our Integrated Photonics team, working across Massy and Palaiseau at the interface between PIC design, characterization, packaging and system integration.

We are looking for a hands-on Photonic Packaging Engineer to take ownership of our packaging activities, improve existing processes and help make our PIC integration more reliable and reproducible.

Your first priority will be to contribute to ongoing packaging activities, develop and improve assembly processes, and troubleshoot integration challenges alongside our PIC design and characterization teams.

As you grow into the role, you will also have the opportunity to develop new packaging approaches, coordinate technical projects and contribute to building more structured and scalable packaging capabilities.

Why this role matters:

Today, packaging activities involve several members of our team. Having a dedicated engineer will help us accelerate ongoing developments, improve the reproducibility of our processes and strengthen the connection between PIC design, characterization and system integration.

As our PIC platforms evolve, your work will also contribute to developing new integration approaches and preparing our packaging processes for future scale-up.

Requirements

What will you do:

Develop and improve photonic packaging processes:

• Take ownership of ongoing packaging activities and improve existing processes.
• Develop optical coupling, precision alignment and fiber-array attachment methods.
• Work on component assembly, bonding and electrical interconnections.
• Address mechanical and thermal integration challenges.
• Test new approaches, troubleshoot issues and improve process reproducibility.

Qualify and improve packaged devices:

• Build and test prototypes to validate packaging approaches.
• Define performance metrics, tolerances and acceptance criteria.
• Characterize packaged PICs alongside the PIC Characterization team.
• Troubleshoot optical, electrical and mechanical integration issues.
• Establish repeatable procedures and technical documentation.

Connect packaging with PIC design:

• Work closely with PIC Designers to anticipate packaging constraints.
• Translate assembly challenges into practical design-for-packaging guidelines.
• Collaborate with characterization and system-integration teams to improve packaged device performance.

Build the packaging capability:

• Collaborate with external packaging partners and equipment suppliers.
• Improve existing equipment, assembly methods and internal capabilities.
• Explore new packaging technologies and integration approaches.
• Support automation to improve accuracy, reproducibility and throughput.
• Progressively lead technical projects and contribute to future scale-up.

How you'll grow:

0–3 months → Get familiar with our PIC platforms, existing packaging processes and integration challenges. Contribute to ongoing activities and start taking ownership of selected technical tasks.

3–6 months → Take increasing responsibility for packaging processes, develop and test improvements, and contribute to making our assembly methods more reliable and reproducible.

6–12 months → Lead packaging development activities within your area of expertise, strengthen our qualification and documentation practices, and contribute to new packaging approaches and technical projects.

Longer term → Depending on your experience and interests, grow into a broader technical role, leading packaging projects, strengthening external partnerships and helping shape our future packaging capabilities.

--

What we're looking for:

Must-have:

• Master's or PhD in Photonics, Physics, Engineering, Microelectronics or related fields.
• Hands-on experience in photonic, optoelectronic or semiconductor packaging.
• Practical experience in optical alignment, component assembly or related processes.
• Good understanding of packaging tolerances, process development and qualification.
• Ability to troubleshoot integration issues and develop reliable packaging solutions.
• Professional English.

Important, but you can grow here

• Fiber-array / FAU attachment and fiber-to-chip coupling
• Wire bonding, flip-chip integration or other electrical interconnection techniques.
• Design for packaging, assembly and manufacturability
• Mechanical and thermal integration
• Experience working with external packaging suppliers or technology partners
• Automation of packaging or precision-assembly processes

Bonus

• Packaging of integrated photonic devices
• Experience with active photonic or optoelectronic components.
• Cryogenic packaging
• High-density electrical interconnection
• Semiconductor production, process-engineering or NPI experience
• Experience developping packaging equipment
• Previous experience coordinating technical projects or leading packaging development activities.

> You do not need previous experience in quantum computing.

> What matters most is your ability to work hands-on with packaging processes, understand integration challenges and help us develop reliable and reproducible solutions.

Benefits

Join a growing quantum hardware company and contribute directly to the development of next-generation photonic quantum processors.

• Take ownership of key PIC packaging activities and processes.
• Develop reliable and reproducible packaging solutions.
• Grow your expertise and contribute to future packaging developments.
• Collaborate with PIC design, characterization and integration teams.
• Work across photonics, semiconductor packaging and quantum hardware.

title: Senior AI Data Engineer  (x/f/m)
Network Developer
description:
Senior Network Developer

About Share

Share is the global marketplace for bandwidth. We aggregate telco infrastructure across Africa (fiber routes, subsea capacity, data centers, cloud on-ramps) into a single intelligence layer. That lets ISPs, hyperscalers and AI companies get connectivity where they need it in seconds, not months.

Today, bandwidth is bought and sold through slow, private, one-off deals, with almost no price transparency. We're replacing that with one neutral exchange: an API on top of real infrastructure, with prices set by actual supply and demand. It's already live across East Africa, with thousands of kilometers of fiber, 12 infrastructure providers, 10 data centers, and around 8 million people served.

The Role

Our network is the foundation of the product. Every route a customer provisions through our API has to exist, perform and stay up on real hardware. We're hiring a Senior Network Developer to design and build that network as software: a distributed, multi-provider fabric that engineers change through code, not by logging into devices.

You'll own the network architecture end to end. That covers our BGP edge (transit, peering at KIXP and LINX, private interconnects with hyperscalers), the backbone, and the PoPs and data centers we're adding across the continent. You'll set the standards our network is built to, which partner ISPs connecting to us will inherit. As we grow, you'll also help build the network engineering team.

What you'll do

  • Design the backbone and PoP architecture as standard, repeatable building blocks, from edge to data center, so we can add capacity and new markets without redesigning each time.

  • Drive our move to Segment Routing and a clean IP architecture, including IPv4 reuse, IPv6, and how customer and internal address space coexist.

  • Build on disaggregated white-box hardware (Edgecore with IP Infusion OcNOS today), and make the hardware and software calls that keep us fast and affordable.

  • Turn operations into software. That means a source of truth (Nautobot), templated config (Jinja), and CI/CD with validation, staged rollouts and rollback for every change.

  • Build the telemetry and observability that show what the network is really doing. Use AI where it actually helps: anomaly detection, automated triage, and auto-remediation with a human in the loop.

  • Own availability. Limit how much any failure can affect, mitigate first and diagnose second, and turn post-mortems into fixes in the system.

  • Work with our software team on the API and provisioning layer that exposes the network to customers, and with partner ISPs' engineers on the hand-off.

  • Help hire and develop the engineers who'll run this with you.

Our Ideal Candidate

  • 8+ years building and operating large networks at a hyperscaler, CDN, internet exchange, carrier or ISP.

  • Deep BGP at scale: route policy, communities, RPKI, traffic engineering, peering and transit.

  • Strong data center and backbone design. You know Clos/EVPN-VXLAN fabrics and MPLS or Segment Routing, and when each makes sense.

  • Hands-on with white-box or disaggregated networking, including choosing hardware and knowing where the silicon limits you.

  • You treat the network as code. You write automation yourself (Python or similar), and you've built or run the pipelines, source of truth and telemetry that make that safe.

  • You've owned availability for something that couldn't go down, and can walk us through a real incident: what broke, how you found it, and what you changed.

  • AI-native in how you work. You've built with these tools, not just used them, and you have a view on where they help in operations and where they don't.

  • You think like an owner. You bring ideas, not tickets, and you want to help build a team, not just a network.

  • A clear, direct communicator who's comfortable with partners' engineers and with our founders.

Nice to have

  • Experience at an internet exchange, or running peering at scale.

  • Open networking stacks like SONiC, OcNOS or FRR, or contributions to them.

  • Streaming telemetry (gNMI/gRPC, sFlow), and building your own monitoring tooling.

  • 400G/800G and optical (ZR) deployments, including vendor selection and certification.

  • Access networks (GPON/XGS-PON) and MikroTik or Huawei gear, since many partner ISPs run it.

  • Building networks in emerging markets such as Africa or Latin America.

  • DDoS mitigation at the edge.

If you don't tick every box but have built and run large networks in production, apply anyway.

Compensation & Benefits

Competitive salary and meaningful equity in a venture-backed company (US-incorporated, with a Kenya operating entity)

title: Enseignante Chercheuse ou Enseignant Chercheur (Maître de conférences)  Qualité des Environnements Intérieurs en CDI à IMT Nord Europe
description:
INTITULÉ : « Qualité des Environnements Intérieurs ».

SPÉCIALITÉS : « Qualité de l'air intérieur, Physico-chimie de l'air, Performance énergétique et environnementale des bâtiments ».

ÉTABLISSEMENT D'AFFECTATION :

École Nationale Supérieure Mines-Télécom Lille Douai dont le nom d'usage est IMT Nord Europe.

Direction / Service : Centre d'Enseignement, de Recherche et d'Innovation Énergie Environnement (CERI EE)

Responsable hiérarchique : Directrice du CERI Énergie Environnement

Catégorie : Agent de catégorie A ou contractuel cadre de gestion de catégorie II

Nature du poste : CDI

Lieu de travail : Site de Douai. Des déplacements sur les autres sites de l'École sont à prévoir

CONTEXTE

École sous tutelle du ministère de l'économie, des finances et de la souveraineté industrielle et numérique, et école de l'Institut Mines Télécom, IMT Nord Europe a 3 missions principales : former des ingénieurs responsables aptes à résoudre les grandes problématiques du XXIème siècle ; mener des recherches débouchant sur des innovations à haute valeur ajoutée ; soutenir le développement des territoires notamment en facilitant l'innovation et les créations d'entreprises. Son objectif est de former les ingénieurs de demain, maîtrisant à la fois les technologies numériques et les savoir-faire industriels. Idéalement située au carrefour de l'Europe, à 1 heure de Paris, 30 minutes de Bruxelles et 1h30 de Londres, IMT Nord Europe a l'ambition de devenir un acteur majeur des grandes transformations industrielles, numériques et environnementales du XXIème siècle en combinant, tant dans ses enseignements et que dans sa recherche, les sciences de l'ingénieur et les technologies du digital.

Localisée sur 2 sites principaux d'enseignement et de recherche, à Lille et à Douai, IMT Nord Europe s'appuie sur plus de 20 000m² de laboratoire pour développer un enseignement de haut niveau et une recherche d'excellence dans les domaines suivants :

•      Énergie Environnement

•      Systèmes Numériques

•      Matériaux et Procédés

L'École dispose également d'antennes à Dunkerque, Valenciennes et Alençon.

Pour plus de détails, consulter le site internet de l'Ecole : www.imt-nord-europe.fr

Le poste est à pourvoir au sein du Centre d'Enseignement, de Recherche et d'Innovation Énergie Environnement (CERI EE) (https://recherche.imt-nord-europe.fr/energie-environnement-ceri/).

Le CERI EE développe des activités au cœur des transitions énergétiques et environnementales. Sa recherche est orientée vers les sciences de l'atmosphère, la qualité des environnements intérieurs et les enjeux de l'efficacité énergétique et de la décarbonation. Le CERI est structuré en trois axes thématiques : EFT (Énergie, Fluides et Transferts), OSPA (Observations, Sources et Processus physico-chimiques Atmosphériques) et QEI (Qualité des Environnements Intérieurs).

L'axe thématique QEI porte sur l'étude, l'identification et la caractérisation des sources de polluants dans les espaces clos et/ou confinés, l'analyse des interactions entre l'air intérieur et les matériaux, ainsi que l'étude de l'influence des environnements sur l'exposition et le bien-être des occupants. Les enjeux scientifiques traités couvrent plusieurs échelles, depuis l'intégration de matériaux et de systèmes énergétiques innovants jusqu'à leurs impacts sur les espaces intérieurs et leurs occupants. Dans un contexte marqué par le changement climatique et des exigences croissantes en termes de QEI et d'efficacité énergétique, une attention particulière est portée aux stratégies d'adaptation et d'atténuation, ainsi qu'aux rôles du comportement des occupants et des différentes sources d'exposition.

Ce poste vise à renforcer et développer l'axe thématique QEI au sein du CERI. La QEI intègre l'étude de multiples paramètres de confort (température, hygrométrie, bruit, luminosité) et de composition de l'air dans les environnements clos (logements, espaces de travail, transports, etc.), afin d'assurer bien-être et santé des occupants. Ces environnements doivent concilier les transitions environnementales et énergétiques avec la qualité de l'air et le confort des occupants.

L'ambition est de consolider le positionnement d'IMT Nord Europe dans ce domaine, avec une synergie entre recherche et formation. Il s'agit de renforcer un réseau de recherche et d'enseignement interdisciplinaire sur cette thématique en réponse à des attentes sociétales, des pouvoirs publics et des acteurs socio-économiques. Le recrutement s'effectue sur un projet de recherche et d'enseignement porté par un ou une titulaire de doctorat et s'inscrivant dans cette stratégie.

Dans ce cadre, IMT Nord Europe recrute un Enseignant Chercheur ou une Enseignante Chercheuse dont les missions sont décrites ci-après.

MISSIONS :

Sous l'autorité de la directrice du CERI EE, le ou la titulaire du poste participera aux activités d'enseignement, de recherche et de transfert de technologie :

Activités de recherche et de transfert de technologie :

Dans le cadre général de la stratégie scientifique précédemment décrite, les recherches auront pour objectif de développer des connaissances scientifiques et des outils avec pour finalité l'amélioration de la qualité de l'air des environnements intérieurs (en particulier mais de manière non exclusive dans les bâtiments), de la santé, du confort et de l'exposition des occupants tout en accompagnant les transformations du cadre bâti nécessaires à la transition écologique et énergétique.

Les thèmes de recherche attendus pourraient porter sur :

•      La préservation de la QEI face au changement climatique et à la nécessaire adaptation à ce changement ;

•      Les contributions des environnements intérieurs à l'exposition des occupants en intégrant les moyens d'évaluation et d'optimisation de l'exposition et du confort des occupants ;

•      Les impacts de la sobriété énergétique des systèmes énergétiques innovants et durables sur la QEI.

La personne recrutée devra :

•      Développer une activité de recherche de haut niveau dans le domaine de la QEI,

•      Initier, conduire et coordonner des projets de recherche régionaux, nationaux et à terme européens,

•      Développer des actions de recherche contractuelle et de transfert de technologie en partenariat avec des acteurs du monde socio-économique,

•      Créer des passerelles entre les axes thématiques du CERI EE et les autres CERI en lien avec les domaines d'excellence d'IMT Nord Europe et de l'Institut Mines Télécom,

•      Encadrer des doctorants, des post-doctorants et des étudiants de Master,

•      Préparer une Habilitation à Diriger des Recherches,

•      Participer au rayonnement de la thématique en lien étroit avec les autres collègues du CERI, notamment à l'international,

•      Publier dans les conférences et revues de référence du domaine, et participer à l'organisation d'événements scientifiques.

Activités d'enseignement :

Le CERI EE intervient dans l'ensemble des cursus Ingénieur. Il porte notamment deux des huit parcours de spécialité de l'école : GE (Génie Energétique) et GERI (Génie de l'Environnement et Risques Industriels) en formation initiale et une formation en apprentissage en Génie Energétique. Le CERI EE est également porteur de deux Mastères Spécialisés (MS) : le MS Bâtiment à Energie Positive, et le MS en Management des Risques Professionnels et Technologiques. Le CERI EE assure également des activités d'enseignements en formation continue, notamment en lien avec la QEI. Enfin, le CERI EE a pour projet de développer à court terme un projet de Master International « Engineering of Sustainable and Healthy Built Environment » dans lequel la personne recrutée viendra en appui aux personnes en charge du développement de cette formation.

La personne recrutée devra :

•      En lien avec le montage en cours d'un Master International Engineering of Sustainable and Healthy Built Environment, proposer un projet d'enseignement qui viendra, en partie, en appui des pilotes de ce Master pour notamment :

–     Contribuer à la finalisation pédagogique et à la promotion de cette nouvelle formation,

–     Contribuer aux enseignements et tutorats des étudiants du master. En s'appuyant sur l'alliance européenne EuLiST, ce Master vise à aligner activités de recherche et d'enseignement. Ces enseignements devront être dispensés en anglais.

•      Contribuer aux activités d'enseignement dans les différentes formations proposées à l'Ecole, dans son domaine de spécialité (QEI) et dans des domaines connexes (ex : chimie, thermodynamique, ...) en fonction de son champ disciplinaire ;

•      Contribuer aux activités pédagogiques sur l'ensemble des formations portées par IMT Nord Europe, en fonction de ses domaines d'expertise et des besoins pédagogiques ;

•      Contribuer à la mise en place d'innovations pédagogiques intégrant les outils numériques (MOOC, classe inversée, etc.),

•      S'investir dans les activités d'encadrement pédagogique (projets, stages, tutorats) et de sélection (concours).


PROFIL : (Prérequis/ Diplôme)

La personne retenue devra être titulaire d'un doctorat et justifier d'une expérience de recherche dans le domaine de la Qualité des Environnements Intérieurs ou dans une discipline contribuant à son étude, telle que la physico-chimie de l'air intérieur, l'évaluation de l'exposition individuelle, ou encore la performance énergétique et environnementale des bâtiments. Le profil recherché repose avant tout sur de solides compétences expérimentales, complété par une bonne compréhension des enjeux et des outils de simulation de la qualité de l'air intérieur. Ainsi, une aptitude à développer des recherches aux interfaces disciplinaires est recherchée afin d'articuler les problématiques d'exposition et de confort des occupants avec les caractéristiques des bâtiments et les stratégies d'amélioration de leur performance énergétique.

Il est attendu du candidat ou de la candidate de :

•      Démontrer une capacité à appréhender les enjeux multidisciplinaires liés à la QEI, avec une ouverture scientifique permettant d'intégrer des problématiques variées et de travailler aux interfaces disciplinaires ;

•      Faire preuve d'une aptitude à développer de nouvelles compétences dans des champs disciplinaires complémentaires à son profil initial ;

•      Posséder une bonne compréhension des enjeux industriels et sociétaux liés aux thématiques du poste ;

•      Attester d'une activité scientifique de qualité, traduite par des publications dans des revues et conférences à fort impact, idéalement en collaboration avec des équipes internationales ;

•      Présenter, si possible, une expérience dans le montage et la conduite de projets financés sur appels à projets compétitifs, avec obtention de financements externes ou démontrer une aptitude à coordonner des actions collectives ;

•      Montrer une appétence pour la transmission des connaissances et l'enseignement en démontrant si possible une expérience en termes d'innovations pédagogiques (MOOC, enseignement hybride, méthodes actives) ;

•      Faire preuve de compétences organisationnelles et relationnelles de manière à interagir efficacement avec l'ensemble des interlocuteurs (enseignement, recherche, support technique et autres partenaires industriels notamment) ;

•      Faire preuve d'autonomie, d'initiative, d'esprit collectif et d'un sens affirmé du service public ;

•      Disposer de solides compétences en communication scientifique et en vulgarisation, en français comme en anglais.

Une expérience internationale, une participation à des projets collaboratifs ainsi qu'un premier réseau au sein des communautés académiques et/ou industrielles constitueront des atouts appréciés. La préparation de l'HDR s'inscrira dans la perspective de l'évolution de carrière de la personne recrutée.

La résidence administrative est fixée à Douai. Des déplacements réguliers sont à prévoir sur l'ensemble des implantations de l'école notamment pour l'enseignement mais aussi de manière plus générale au national et à l'international dans le cadre des activités de recherche.
